neighbours.label: About to name a physical mishap: something spilled, knocked over or damaged by accident
fire: A barge struck the pier at dawn, spilling diesel into the harbour.
The busboy slipped on the wet tiles and the glasses crashed to the floor.
Felt pads shield your tabletop from scratches and stains.
Strap the ladder down so it won't be knocked off the roof rack.
The toddler bumped the table and the juice went all over the rug.
A pipeline ruptured in the marsh, spewing oil over the reeds.
Wrap each plate in paper to guard against chips and cracks.
The jar slipped from her wet hands, spilling pickles across the kitchen.
quiet: A ferry reached the pier at dawn, unloading diesel for the harbour.
The waiter walked across the clean tiles and set the glasses on the shelf.
Those coasters come in several colours and sizes for your tabletop.
Put a helmet on before you climb up to the roof.
The little girl sat at the table and drank her juice beside the rug.
A long canal runs through the marsh, carrying boats past the reeds.
Wrap each gift in paper to give at the wedding reception.
The jar sat on the shelf beside the pickles in the pantry.

notes: The card leads with ' sp' of spilling and spewing, but also fires on against, from and being before the damage is named. Probing: 'tripped and' fired hard. The + pole looks like violent motion rather than a clean opposite, so it is not claimed.
